newsitem.title: JAPAN: THANONG SAYS NOT ASKING JAPAN BANKS FOR NEW LOANS.
newsitem.headline: THANONG SAYS NOT ASKING JAPAN BANKS FOR NEW LOANS.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said as he entered a meeting with Japanese bankers on Tuesday that he had never thought of asking Japanese private banks at the meeting to extend new loans.
Asked if he would call for new loans from Japanese private banks, Thanong told Reuters: "I have never thought about it, but it may probably come later."

Thanong was meeting with representatives of 21 major Japanese commercial banks a day after a multilateral conference in Tokyo agreed to provide $16 billion to help overcome a financial crisis in Thailand.
Bankers attending Tuesday's meeting told Reuters that the International Monetary Fund and the Thai minister were expected to explain to the meeting the package that had been agreed on Monday.
One banker, asked if the Japanese banks would provide new loans to Thailand if requested, said his bank had not thought about it.
Thanong said on Monday that Thailand's foreign debt stood at $89 billion. Japanese banks are estimated to be owed about half that amount.
